meta.title: Sorun.dev — Coworking technology audits
meta.description: Independent technology audits for coworking spaces. WiFi, access control, management platform, meeting rooms — assessed, prioritised, and explained in plain language.

hero.label: Coworking technology advisory
hero.headline: You run the space. We map the tech.
hero.subheadline: Coworking is a hospitality business with a network closet. We audit the systems that run your space — from WiFi and access control to your management platform. One fixed price. One clear roadmap.
hero.cta_sub: No commitment. No sales pitch. A conversation about your space.

problem.label: The problem

scenarios.s1: The WiFi drops on a Tuesday morning. A member tweets about it.
scenarios.s2: The door reader fails. Staff have to let people in manually.
scenarios.s3: Platform data doesn't sync. You're re-entering every invoice.

problem.long_paragraph: Recurring WiFi complaints lead to churn. Broken access control wastes your staff's time. Manual processes that should be automated eat hours every week. Most coworking spaces are running on technology decisions that made sense at setup but no longer fit how the space actually operates — and by the time it breaks, it has already cost you members, revenue, and reputation.
problem.positive_bridge: There's a way out — but it isn't more enterprise software, more vendors, or more meetings.
problem.fit_paragraph: The help that exists does not fit. Enterprise integrators are too expensive. General IT support does not understand your operations. Software vendors only care about their own platform. You need someone who understands the full stack and the business it supports.
problem.empathy: We know how exhausting it is to fight your tech every Monday morning. Coworking is a hospitality business with a network closet — and your members judge you on the WiFi.
problem.closing: Most spaces grow faster than their infrastructure. By the time it breaks, it has already cost you members, revenue, and reputation.

layers.label: What we audit
layers.headline: The 8 layers of workspace technology.
layers.subheadline: Every coworking space runs on these eight systems. We assess all of them — and how they connect.

network.name: Network infrastructure
network.description: WiFi access points, switches, cabling, ISP, and network segmentation

access.name: Access control
access.description: Door hardware, fobs, mobile access, controllers, and intercom

platform.name: Space management platform
platform.description: Memberships, billing, bookings, member app, and reporting

meeting.name: Meeting room systems
meeting.description: AV equipment, displays, booking panels, and videoconferencing

security.name: Security & CCTV
security.description: Cameras, recording, retention, monitoring, and access to footage

telephony.name: Telephony & front of house
telephony.description: VoIP, intercom, reception hardware, and PA systems

integrations.name: Integrations & automation
integrations.description: System connections, workflows, APIs, and manual handoffs

devices.name: IT & device management
devices.description: Staff devices, printers, member-facing tech, and IT support

process.label: The methodology
process.headline: From first call to final report in 2–3 weeks.

intake.title: Intake call
intake.deliverable: A one-page scope summary in your inbox the same day.

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.deliverable: A technology footprint document showing where each system lives.

inventory.title: Stack inventory
inventory.deliverable: Complete stack inventory — typically 40–60 pages, indexed by layer.

assessment.title: Assessment
assessment.deliverable: Prioritised findings matrix with cost / effort / impact ratings.

report.title: Report & walkthrough
report.deliverable: Full written report + executive summary + 90-day roadmap + recording.

deliverables.label: What you receive
deliverables.headline: A clear picture and a plan to fix it.

report.title: Full written report
report.description: A detailed document covering all 8 layers of your technology infrastructure. Plain language. No jargon.

findings.title: Prioritised findings
findings.description: Every finding categorised: act now, high priority, 90-day plan, and future consideration.

roadmap.title: Implementation roadmap
roadmap.description: A sequenced plan showing what to fix first, what it will cost, and how long it will take.

deliverables.note: Every audit includes a 60-minute live walkthrough where we present findings to your team and answer questions. Recorded for anyone who couldn't make it.
deliverables.sample_sub: Email us and we'll send you an anonymised excerpt by return.

credibility.label: Track record
credibility.headline: Built on the operations side. Brought to advisory.
credibility.testimonial_quote: We thought our tech was 'mostly fine.' The audit found €18k of avoidable spend in our first year and three reasons our members keep mentioning the WiFi. The roadmap paid for itself before week six.
credibility.testimonial_attribution: — Operations lead, independent flex space (5 locations, NL)
credibility.testimonial_note: Anonymised at client's request. Full case studies available on request.

geography.question: Do you work outside the Netherlands?
geography.answer: Yes. The audit is delivered 100% remotely, so geography rarely matters. Most engagements have been in the Benelux and DACH regions, with a handful in Southern Europe.

smallest.question: What's the smallest space you'll audit?
smallest.answer: We work with single-location spaces from ~30 desks upward. Below that the cost of an audit isn't proportional to the value — but we're happy to point you to lighter-weight resources.

multisite.question: How does pricing work for multi-site operators?
multisite.answer: The €1,500 figure is a single-location entry tier. For multi-site engagements, shared infrastructure (network, platform, integrations) is audited once across the portfolio, with site-specific layers (access control, AV, CCTV) added per location. Quoted per portfolio.

not_included.question: What's NOT included?
not_included.answer: We don't implement, install, or fix things ourselves. The audit ends with a roadmap; from there you choose to execute in-house, with one of our vetted partners, or with us coordinating end-to-end (a separate engagement).

timing.question: When can you start?
timing.answer: Typically 2–3 weeks from kickoff. We're currently booking engagements ~6 weeks out. Ask on the intro call for the next available slot.

remote.question: Do you need to visit on-site?
remote.answer: No. The audit is built around remote delivery — floor plans, photos, walkthrough videos, and async questions. On-site visits are available as an add-on for very complex layouts but rarely change the findings.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: Sorun ("we", "us") respects your privacy. This page describes what data we collect when you visit sorun.dev or engage us for an audit, why we collect it, how we handle it, and your rights under the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

controller.heading: Data controller
controller.body: The data controller for sorun.dev is Sorun.dev. For all privacy-related questions, contact hello@sorun.dev.

what.heading: What we collect
what.body: When you visit the site we store two values in your browser's localStorage: your theme preference (light/dark) and your language preference (en/nl/es). These never leave your browser. When you book an intro call we use Cal.com, which collects the information you choose to provide (name, email, time slot). When you email us at hello@sorun.dev we receive your email content and address. We do not run advertising trackers, fingerprinting scripts, or third-party analytics that identify individuals.

legal.heading: Legal basis
legal.body: Browser preferences are stored under the legitimate interest of providing the service you requested (a working website). Booking and email communications are processed under your consent and to enter into / perform a contract.

subprocessors.heading: Sub-processors
subprocessors.body: Cal.com Inc. (US) — used for scheduling intro calls. Cal.com signs the EU Standard Contractual Clauses for transfers outside the EEA. Hosting provider — to be specified at deployment.

retention.heading: Retention
retention.body: Browser preferences persist until you clear your localStorage. Email correspondence is retained for the duration of the engagement plus 7 years for tax/audit purposes. Booking metadata held by Cal.com follows their retention policy.

rights.heading: Your rights
rights.body: Under GDPR you have the right to access, correct, delete, restrict, port, or object to processing of your personal data, and to lodge a complaint with your supervisory authority (in the Netherlands, the Autoriteit Persoonsgegevens). To exercise any of these, email hello@sorun.dev.

changes.heading: Changes
changes.body: We will update this page if our practices change. The "last updated" date at the top reflects the current version.
